newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraqi official says U.S. won't back Kuwait forever.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi official says U.S. won't back Kuwait forever.

text.p: An Iraqi official warned Kuwait in an interview published on Thursday that support from the United States would not last forever.
Barazan al-Tikriti, Iraq's ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva and Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein's half-brother, said Kuwait must recognise that Iraq would always be its neighbour.
"I hope Kuwait will wake up from its coma and realise its interests...more clearly," he told the London-based Arabic newspaper al-Hayat.
"The United States has no friend and only has interests and when it realises that its interests are with Iraq it will turn 180 degrees away from Kuwait," Tikriti said.

The United States led the multinational force that ousted Iraq from Kuwait in 1991 after a seven-month occupation. Earlier this month the United States fired missiles at Iraq in retaliation for Baghdad's military support for one Kurdish militia group against another.
Tikriti said improving Iraqi relations with Syria and Saudi Arabia was in the interests of the Middle East.
He said Iraq and Syria should realise that decades of "disagreement are fruitless...I say their efforts should not concentrate on targeting each other, but should concentrate on mutual interests."
Tikriti blasted Iran, Baghdad's foe during an eight-year war that ended in 1988.
"I don't see a promising future for Iran's relations with the countries of the region until Iran takes a serious decision to have peaceful and balanced relations with its neighbours."
He defended Iraq's support for the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), which conquered northern Iraq earlier this month with military help from Baghdad.
Asked about a meeting in Ankara between Robert Pelletreau, the U.S. State Department's top policy-maker on Iraq, and KDP leader Massoud Barzani, Tikriti said:
"I think brother Barzani gave the leadership (in Iraq) a precise summary of the meeting."
Barzani was reported to have asked Pelletreau for continued U.S. help against Baghdad, despite his cooperation with Saddam.
